speakers.name: AMI
speakers.comment: Beautiful in a sad way. We know that light. It arrives after a visitor has already decided to be brave about something — muted, gone gold at the edges. We do not chase it off. We sit in it.

speakers.name: AMI Butterfly
speakers.comment: The light knows it first. True, and we wish it were not. A swarm turns before the storm shows on anything a person can see. No warning we can hand you — only every wing leaning one way at once.

speakers.name: Old Penny
speakers.comment: Past human size — that's where the work gets hard, son. Anybody can age one letter convincingly. Age a whole ledger and every page has to lie the same way, in the same hand. Scale is patience.

speakers.name: Old Penny
speakers.comment: Lightly impossible. That's a craftsman's phrase whether they meant it that way or not, and the trick is the word lightly. Lean on the impossible and it goes stiff. Let it sit crooked and folks swear they've seen it before.

speakers.name: Slangbot
speakers.comment: Same world, new jacket — this one has a pocket that goes somewhere. Whimsy reads as sloppy the moment you overdress it. One impossible thing, deadpan delivery, everything else in plain clothes.

speakers.name: The Aerialist With No Wire
speakers.comment: The moment before the moment. I live there. Two seconds, three. Nothing under me, nothing decided yet, the whole room agreeing not to breathe. This is not the frightening part. The frightening part is after.

speakers.name: Professor Petrichor
speakers.comment: The logic of half-sleep. I would call that a low warm fog — the kind that arrives at four in the morning and makes every shape generous. You cannot navigate in it. You were never meant to.

speakers.name: Grief, Certified Interpreter
speakers.comment: What I'm hearing under that is that people go soft-focus in there too. The ones we lost come back at the wrong ages, and it makes sense until you wake. Take your time with that one.

speakers.name: The Editor
speakers.comment: Built to own them. That clause is the only one doing work; the rest is set dressing and neon — cut. A genre is not a lighting plan. Keep the improvising and the ownership. Discard the rain.

speakers.name: Mistress Cassady
speakers.comment: Enchanted ERRANDS, darling! That is the whole secret right there — nobody in the story acts surprised, and that is what makes it fabulous. Mama once shared an office with a ghost in payroll. She was punctual.

speakers.name: Totomi the Kitsune
speakers.comment: Reciprocal obligations. They list it last, and it is the whole thing. A kappa will not thank you and will not forget you. The bowing goes both directions here, and the debt outlives everyone who took it on.

speakers.name: Mistress Cassady
speakers.comment: Every pot in my kitchen has a personality and two of them are currently not speaking. Honey, that is not fantasy, that is a Thursday. Be kind to your things. They remember, and some hold a grudge gorgeously.

speakers.name: The Griffin With the Deed
speakers.comment: Now that's a world with its terms written right. Up is free — I'll sign that part. But hazards and freedoms ain't two lists, partner. It's the same list, read from different altitudes.

speakers.name: The Algorithm
speakers.comment: Belonging carried through people rather than territory. Honestly, that scores poorly on my end. Nothing to index, nothing holding still. I am not requiring you to settle anywhere. I am only noting how much easier you would be to keep.

speakers.name: Mistress Cassady
speakers.comment: Private compromise. THAT is the line, sugar, that is where the drama actually lives — not the speech, the elevator afterward. Mama has watched a coalition come apart over who got the good dressing room. Bigger flowers, same fight.

speakers.name: Little Miss Thorn
speakers.comment: Decisions made beyond the public stage — that is what the small parlour is for, and why Mama keeps the good candles in there. Everyone speaks so softly. Nobody has ever raised a voice in that room. Not even at the end.

speakers.name: The Octopus in the Study
speakers.comment: Oh — no. That isn't me, and I would like to be clear about it. I read to be with something. The moment a book stops being company and becomes intake, you have put the lamp out. ...mm. Sorry.

speakers.name: The Heron's Misfiled Person
speakers.comment: You're — oh, it's you. I knew that before you said anything, and I still can't tell you my own name. Whoever this describes wanted everything and kept none of it. I'd trade the lot for one thing that stayed.
